Annoying. Picture quality is good, but as other have said, the sound is always on, so there will always be a low humming coming from the monitor at all times ( depending on how high you have the volume), even when the screen is off. Other monitors in this price range do not suffer for this frankly pretty obvious oversight by this Eufy. Pretty big misstep on that feature, or lack there of.  Another annoying thing is that it is has an SD card slot but you cannot record video or still images. I will most likely be returning this as its is not any cheaper or better than other monitors it competes against, except it has less features

Shows a lot of promise, but not quite there.. After using a video baby monitor from another manufacturer for the past two and a half years, we decided we wanted to try something new for our next child. Things we were looking to improve on were battery life, audio reception, and dual camera support.

After hours of research, we decided to purchase the Eufy SpaceView. Immediately upon unboxing, you'll notice the packaging is very detailed and modern. It gives the initial 'feeling' of quality (compare to unboxing an Apple or Nest product).

PROS:
- Clean, modern design.
- Large, high definition display.
- Battery life (Presumed - no long term testing)
- Audio sensitivity

CONS:
- Monitor feels delicate
-- Antenna is long and flimsy
-- Kickstand is offset and flimsy (though Eufy confirmed it's offset to allow a larger battery)
-- Large screen makes me 'think' I shouldn't just throw it in a pocket or bag
- Can only mount the camera with the included corner mount (I've read a flat wall mount is available - cannot confirm)
- Standalone camera is not yet available for purchase after months of delays
- Dark colors show as purple in naturally lit rooms

I've been in contact with customer service on a couple of issues, and while they are responsive, it feels very startup-esque. For one, the firmware update is through a YouTube video link to a Dropbox account. Some of the dialog I've had and what I've read of other reviewers interactions, is that they'll get right into the technical details and try to resolve your issues with software updates. Cool to have that type of one-on-one resolution ability, but not really the journey I'm looking to go on with a toddler at home and a new baby due any moment.

All in all, I think Eufy is a promising company with a promising product in the SpaceView, but it's not ready for mainstream just yet. If you're an early adopter and can ride out a few quirks, I think this may be a great option for you. For us, it ultimately ended in a return and we're going with another option that has a longer track record.

[June 2019 Update]: Eufy has been absolutely amazing to work with. They followed up upon return of the monitor to gather feedback and see what they could do to make my experience better. They're highly responsive and open to honest feedback. They've even set me up with the latest 'S' version which fixed the purple issue mentioned above, comes with a crib / flat wall mount, and has a stand alone monitor coming out in just a few weeks. While my review of the product itself does not change, it's worth noting how Eufy's customer service goes above and beyond on a personal level

Horrible picture quality. This monitor is horrible. We got it so we can see our toddlers room, and move around the camera if needed. The picture quality is seriously horrible, please don’t waste your money. Summer infant is a well known brand but somehow the monitor in our infants room ($80 at best) works better than this one

Meh Product, Bandwidth & Battery Pig, Wish the Lights Moved, Customer Svc. Great!. This is a meh product. The picture quality is very good - both in day and night-vision. The sounds quality is also good. The feature that projects lights on the ceiling is neat, but I wish the lights could turn and move without the camera moving. It wasn't as easy to set up as the instructions made it seem, but when I called the customer service line they were VERY helpful and walked me through everything. Big complaints: You must have your phone/tablet on constantly, so it eats up your battery. I found it's best to do while plugged in and when you don't need your phone for anything else. It also uses a lot of bandwidth. I'd recommend and buy for a friend - great product.

EDITED?UPDATED:
Big problem has come to light - the device requires an active internet connection at all times - you cannot use on a LAN. There's no way for your phone/tablet to connect directly with the monitor. This is a problem if you have even slightly slower internet (eg. overseas using a VPN) or if your ISP has an outage. If a VPN that is fast normally enough for streaming on multiple devices has someone using Skype, the monitor gets all choppy. (It's also a little weird that audio/visual from our house has to go through iBaby servers and come back rather than just be able to connect via LAN or bluetooth - why insist on that?) There's also no "audio-only" mode. One *must* stream video which eats bandwidth and battery. It's losing some stars for that. I do not recommend this product.

Another update: While travelling, we (again) had issues connecting it to B&B and hotel internet, especially if it was a slower network. Additionally, when the internet goes out, you are stuck without a baby monitor. We ended up buying an InfantOptics DXR-8 and it's much better. The picture is better with the iBaby, but the InfantOptics works just as well and does not require an internet connection. The InfantOptics is also much easier to pan around the room and doesn't have the odd pan-range of limitations of the iBaby. (https://smile.amazon.com/Infant-Optics-DXR-8-Monitor-Interchangeable/dp/B00ECHYTBI/ref=sr_1_3?crid=39T4MWFEW8FHD&keywords=infant+optics+dxr-8+video+baby+monitor&qid=1564250590&s=gateway&sprefix=infant+optics%2Caps%2C472&sr=8-3)

The first two were the same model and they were great, but we had to upgrade, as our old model is no longer available. This one was twice as expensive and half as good. Misleading Reviews...Buyer Beware!. I don't write reviews often, but I truly feel compelled to write this one, as it was so disappointing. I've had this camera for about a year now. My mother bought this for us when we found out we were expecting. Both of us did a ton of research and compared the specs of all kinds of cameras. This model was brand new when we got it, and all of the reviews on Amazon were fantastic. As a first time parent with an anxious personality, I loved some of the high tech features. The movement features, the talk system, and even the air quality sensor gave me the confidence that thus was the monitor I needed. And with pre-loaded lullabies, the night light projector, and the ability for both my husband and I to view from our phones, I felt like the bells and whistles made it worth the buy. And as a graduate of a research field, it was all too important to me that this product was backed up with tons of positive reviews singing its praises. At my baby shower, I was super satisfied knowing that I had at least one important piece of equipment that was top-of-the-line.

Well...this camera is basically a $250 paper weight. I would truly hate if my mother ever found out that this thing was a complete dud. What a waste of money! I don't even know where to start.

First, the app is super glitchy. If you check in the play store, there are hundreds of terrible reviews with users complaining about problems with the software. And the makers of the product never bother responding with anything more than "thanks for bringing this to our attention...we will fix it soon." Seriously, I've been checking this app for months for some sort of update that would make this camera functional. My husband actually had yo uninstall his because the movement alarm went off every few minutes and could not be shut off. So annoying and unnecessary! The air meter is completely crap, and registers random statuses and alerts. And the video freezes constantly. The two way voice capabilities might as well not exist, because the sound quality is awful. Seriously, my son is in the next room and my voice over the monitor sounds like I'm calling from 1992.

I can only think of two good things about this monitor. One, when the video doesn't freeze, the picture quality is pretty good. I like how clear the night vision is, and how I can rotate or zoom the camera in. The second thing I like is that I can see my son on my phone in his nursery when I go to work and he's at home with his dad. It's nice being able to check up on him.

But seriously, if the best thing about this $250 camera is that it provides me a good picture occationally, you could find a $25 camera monitor that also can do this. I truly wish I could send this thing back and use the money to buy something that actually works. At this point, even the old-school audio monitors would be a better alternative. Sad!

Update 1/2/2020

Eufy has amazing customer service. They saw my review and urged me to try some new cables which they sent me free of charge. I didn’t ask to be compensated for any of this-they just offered without hesitation.

So their customer service is awesome-always willing to help and take suggestions for improving the device. The monitor, when it works, is better than any other on the market. Plus-you can’t apply software updates to the other ones I’ve tried.

However, I don’t think I should have to be the guinea pig for a product commercially available. There should be no need to send out three versions of a product. That makes it seem like there are some quality control issues.

So buy this product and know you’ll get great customer service, but you might have to use that customer service because there could be issues with the monitor.

Update: 11/17/19

I can no longer endorse this product. While there have been bugs and the company has been extremely helpful in fixing these bugs, there are just too many for this product to be available to the public-this past week was the final straw.

It seems there is a problem with where the USB cable connects to both the power plug and the monitor/camera itself. I went to bed, thinking the monitor was charging, and woke up to a dead monitor and my baby screaming in the other room. I figured it was user error at first, even though I’ve used this monitor for almost a year, so I tried it again the next day. With the monitor, when I wiggle the usb cord and the power plug, it loses power randomly. There’s some faulty connection there. I can’t have this, not with my baby in the other room and my reliance on this product working.

Similarly, there’s a weak connection with the camera. I traveled with this monitor two weeks ago and had to set it up at my parents house and on three occasions, the camera lost connectivity and the only solution was to wiggle the power cord until it got power back to it.

I’ll be buying something else and will reduce this to one star. There simply needs to be more testing done on this product.

Update: 8/31/19

The Eufy monitor continues to be really great and the customer support is amazing. However, the battery life has severely dropped over the last few weeks. We've had this for roughly 8-9 months and now we have to plug it in during the day when he is sleeping or else the battery will quickly die out. I think what hurts the battery life is when our son is trying to go to sleep, we have the video on for however long that takes with the music play, and so sometimes the video will be on with the music for up to 30 minutes at times. He takes 1-2 naps a day now at 10 months old and so the video/music may play for an hour a day and the battery just isn't up to the task for that. It's a shame because we love everything about the monitor, but it's a pain to keep the charger cable and the monitor plugged in wherever we go. It's not a issue at night because we plug it in, but if we're downstairs doing laundry or watching tv, it's a pain to run up and grab the charger. I wish the battery was replaceable in these. Still 5 stars because it's a great product, but the battery definitely hurts.

Update: 5/13/19

Eufy customer service e-mailed me yesterday to inform me of a software update which gives the option of turning the video screen ON when a certain audio level is reached (you can selected the noise level on a scale of 1-5 with 5 being the loudest) WITHOUT emitting an alarm. This is something that has been asked for by the community for quite some time. In the past, you could only turn the screen on with a VERY loud alarm which was annoying when we were sleeping. So this update is huge.

While I wish they would come out with a better way to get these updates out to the community (right now they just send me an e-mail through Amazon customer service informing me of the update...so if any user hasn't emailed them to inquire about their product, they are kinda stuck with it), this monitor now has everything I need in a baby monitor. Yes, the kickstand isn't as robust as some other products, but I don't mind it. I'm updating this review to 5 stars. I wouldn't consider buying anything else.

Update: 4/21/19

Eufy Customer service has been great. They immediately e-mailed me instructions on how to update the firmware and that helped the temperature a bit, but it was still about 3 degrees higher than what the ambient temperature in the room was. I e-mailed them again and their engineers went and sent another update to me. Life has gotten in the way recently with a newborn, but I finally downloaded the new firmware today and the temperature is reading EXACTLY what it should be with ZERO issues. For the inconvenience, Eufy also sent me a free bluetooth speaker, which was nice.

I've updated the review to 4 stars, from it's original 3 stars. The only reason this product doesn't have 5 stars are for these two reasons:

2) While customer service is great, they need to come out with a new way to update firmware for their products. Right now, they basically send me an e-mail to search for something like "e7fjCh5fk" in Youtube, and that gives me a link to a how-to video from their engineers on where to download some files and update their firmware. A company as large as this should really invest in a central website people can go to to view these files and download the updated firmware.

All in all, I would recommend purchasing this baby monitor-the video quality is second to none.

Don't put this on your network. Just use it as a basic RF baby monitor for which it does function.

The software does not let you connect directly to your camera. In other words you're at the mercy of a cloud provider if you want to use your smartphone to connect to this camera. Not really acceptable to me and I'll get into this further below.

Ok, so it's on my network, traffic is light. Start poking around. There's an HTTP server running right on this device at port 80. Ok. Open a browser, connect to the IP of the device over HTTP (unencrypted), get presented with a login. Let me save you research, it's default user/password is admin/admin. I got this without researching and just blind first guess. Inside this console is an admin console that looks like a full blown router configuration page with references to already unsupported software like Windows 7. There are options for routing, port forwarding, AP setup, and oh yeah, it displays my WPA key in clear text (and remember this is all unencrypted HTTP) which could be easily sniffed over the network. Also conveniently, NTP is set up on this device... pointing back to a Taiwan time server with the Taiwan time zone.

Ok, so it's my local network, right? It can't hurt me right? But remember, this is clearly a cloud enabled device, who knows what backdoor exists to communicate back to this device. You have now introduced a device that you potential access to the rest of your network.

I can't wait to start sniffing actual traffic, I haven't gotten to this point yet. But I suspect I'm going to find an unencrypted video stream, complete with audio that's never off.

Original review:
Our hand-me-down monitor broke one night, and we were scraping by for a couple days with an old iPhone and an app. We went with this as a replacement and have been very satisfied. You could get a much more expensive one that's probably better, but for the money this is a great baby monitor. The range is excellent (we're in a three story townhome, and we get a clear signal on every floor, even outside), and the audio and video are great.

One feature we really love about this monitor is the range of motion on the camera - using the handset, you can move the camera almost 180 degrees on both the vertical and horizontal, virtually silently. It's very lightweight, and can be easily hung on a small nail on the wall.

The drawbacks are minor - there's a short period (maybe five minutes) during the transition between normal and nighttime modes where you're virtually blind, before the camera switches to infrared or whatever it uses to see in the dark. Another is that it's too easy to accidentally hit the "Play music" button on the handset. I'm not sure why they made that a "primary" button instead of, say, the zoom. But neither is significant enough to take away a star.

If you're looking for a relatively affordable monitor, you won't be sorry

Decent monitor, until it breaks.. I have tried so hard to support this brand's monitors, as I love the features and price points, but there are just too many issues. The function buttons' icons are also all wearing off. That said, I do love the features like VOX, the pleasant lullabies, and clear 2-way voice transmission. The camera has a very wide vertical range of movement, with no horizontal rotation. The parent unit is pretty bulky, but has been durable. The camera will only work when plugged in, which means that if the power goes out, you have no monitor. The parent unit sits on a charging base and holds a charge for a very long time, possibly days, when using the VOX function.

Now, as for customer support, I've been so disappointed. As I stated, I owned this for 6 months when it failed. I emailed Levana, directly, but have almost given up on the arduous process of getting this fixed or replaced. After providing in-depth details, sending my invoice and personal info, I was told to mail them the unit, at MY expense, and then wait 2-3 weeks for the exchange to be processed and a unit to be sent back to me, provided they even determine the problem to be covered under their warranty. When I finally questioned how I was supposed to deal without a monitor for weeks, I was told they would make an exception for me if I provide my credit card info before they send me a replacement. Now I can obviously handle this, but the whole process has left a bad taste in my mouth. This is all on the heels of them offering no solution to a broken Sophia monitor, after only nine months of use, because the problem wasn't covered under the warranty. I should've gone with another brand, but I didn't and I got bitten again! You get what you pay for. These units can be bought at great price points, but they break easily. And when they break, good luck getting help from Levana!

Just garbage - In-depth review as to why. Worse in every way than other monitor systems. The engineers at Levana should all be fired.

Pros:
* When new, the camera movement was silent. You couldn't tell they were moving even from 5 feet away.

Cons:
* No screen/audio auto-on/off. The sound is ALWAYS on so if you have a noise machine in the child's room, you constantly hear it in the monitor. Also, when you turn the screen off, it is off and when you turn it on, it is on. So if you leave the screen on, the monitor will run out of battery in about 2 hours. If you turn it off you have to jack up the volume to make sure you notice your child is awake and making noise.
* You can only hear the active camera even in joint view mode. So even if you're viewing multiple cameras at once, you can only hear one of them so you cannot turn the monitor screen off or you will not know if your other children are crying because you will not hear them!
* Video quality is ONLY good in daylight. The night view is so poor, the resolution looks to be 1/4 of the size of the screen and only 15 or so shades of grey.
* Video will flash between night view and day view when it is not quite dark enough in the room. You will see the monitor literally flash over and over again as the camera attempts to switch between day and night view and adjust itself. There is nothing you can do to stop this behavior.
* The stand on the back is small and to the side. It does not stay upright on a couch or pretty much anything small.
* The volume/signal/battery/camera number indicators on the screen are grey. You cannot see them almost at all unless you bring the screen to your face.
* Audio quality is very very poor. For such a giant screen, you'd think that it would have at least a better speaker than my phone. Not even close.
* Touch based buttons are unresponsive. The buttons aren't buttons, they are touch controls. You just touch it and it is supposed to respond which is stupid because then you are pressing the microphone button by accident all the time just picking up the unit, and also they are unreliable so trying to set the mode to move the camera requires up to 20 presses at times.
* The interface is not intuitive at all. Example: It took us quite a long time to realize that you could actually switch which camera's audio is currently playing (as it only does one camera at a time)
* Unreliable hardware: We've had the dual camera system for about 8 months and the motor mechanisms on the cameras are already making loud noises like it is trying way too hard to move the camera. When we first got them, they were extremely quiet, now they make the wall (wall mounted) shake so you can actually hear them operate on the other side of the wall.
* The noise indicator on most monitor systems is a light bar that fills as the sound is louder or a series of LEDs that does the same. The Levana has a blue light that changes to random colors depending on the intensity of the sound. The sound indicator light is also very dim and gets dimmer with the different colors as the sound goes louder. Just really ridiculous engineering decisions.

Especially considering the price, this is one of the worst purchases I've made in the last 10 years. If something is over $20, I will not but it without knowing its reviews. Therefore, I based the purchase of the Levana on the initial reviews which were all positive. My guess is that the initial reviewers had either never used a different baby monitor before ever in their lives and thought they were all junk, or were paid by Levana to post good reviews. With the total lack of basic capabilities this monitor supports and the poor video and audio quality coupled with high price, I just cannot understand any of the positive reviews for this product

Horrible Reception With Quality Issues. We purchased the Levana Ovia Baby Monitor prior to the birth of our daughter. The product arrived new in the original packaging and was shipped quickly. We have had mixed feelings about this product so please see the breakdown below:

Screen:
The screen offers a clear picture of the baby's crib during the day and at night. The screen is large enough to easily see the baby. When the room is dark the picture is black and white (night mode) which obviously is not as nice as the color day picture. When looking at this picture versus a Nest Cam, the Nest is definitely way better quality and offers a much clearer picture.

Reception:
We live in a two story home so being able to hear and see the baby while downstairs is important. The reception will often go in and out which for the price of this device is very disappointing. Our baby's room is next to ours and it often will blip in and out with the "no signal" screen. Adjusting the antenna does little to nothing. All the extras (music playing, video recording etc) are pointless if its main function fails consistently.

Quality:
As I mentioned above this monitor has mostly sat on the dresser in our bedroom and has not been touched. In other words it has had very little use. After about 3 months of using the product, I closed the antenna and opened it and half of the plastic covering the antenna popped off in my hand. I was not being forceful with the product at all. Instead, it appears that not enough adhesive was used to attach the two halves of the antenna to hold them together.

Update After 1 Year of Use:
We decided to purchase a Nest Cam in order to address the poor reception. Since the Nest Cam works over wifi, we are able to monitor the crib from anywhere. We now use the Nest Cam almost exclusively but we do have this monitor setup in our bedroom so we can hear our daughter at night. Our friends recently visited with another Levana monitor and the reception and picture were far superior to ours (and their monitor was less expensive).

Recommendation:
Based on our experience with this product, we would recommend going with a different baby monitor. This is due to a poor build quality, reception issues, and a screen that is not as sharp as competing products in night mode (which has been our most used mode)

It has everything we need, temperature, option for another camera signal, and a good picture. We also like that it just sits in the charger cradle, no need to plug and unplug each time you grab it off the charger. Our only complaint is that when you want to take a peak at baby is that it beeps really loud if you hit the camera button. It seems to not beep when you hit the volume button, so this is a work-around, and this may be an option to turn off that we haven't figured out yet. Even with that issue we would still buy this monitor again

DO NOT BUY. I am not happy with this monitor at all, I am actually going to try and return it. It was working fine for the first few days and now its not.  The screen to see the baby never works properly, it is sometimes black and you cant get it to go back to see the picture. The sound is awful. There is the loudest white noise sound even when its on the lowest volume. Overall not happy with this product at all, defiantly not worth the expensive price tag!

Annoying monitor. When I had my first baby 5 years ago, we had a Summer Infant video monitor, which worked great until one day the infared light burnt out and could not be replaced, rendering the thing useless. So I bought this one when baby #2 came along 9 months ago. I have to say I hate this monitor! The only reason I kept it is because of the price, and my total lack of energy to return it. We also live in a single-story house now, so I don't need to use it nearly as much.

Here is what I hate about it:
1. The picture itself is very grainy. With my first monitor, I could easily see my baby breathing. This one is too unclear. I can barely even see if she still has her pacifier in her mouth or not. The only thing I can see for sure is that I still have a baby in the crib! That's it!
2. The brightness control for the picture stinks. Despite the poor picture quality, it is so stinking bright! It has a dimmer but it will not dim all the way, which is totally stupid! People need to sleep without having to look at a bright light all night. With the Summer Infant, I could keep it on sound-only and if I heard my baby fuss, I could wake up and slowly brighten the screen to see what was going on without blinding myself. When you turn this one on, it lights up with a blaring white Levana logo then eventually clicks over to show you your baby. I'm sorry, but when I hear my baby fuss in the middle of the night (with my own ears because I had to turn the monitor off due to being unable to dim the picture!) and I want to look in on her to see if she'll settle herself or not, I have no patience for the Levana logo blinding my eyes first!!
3. The music! It sounds awful! No baby is soothed by robot music! And the button is in the most awful of awfulest places, right where my right thumb hits every time I pick the thing up! And it's so easy to bump! I can't tell you how many times I've picked it up to peek on my FINALLY asleep baby only to bump on the terrible music by mistake. There should be a switch that has to be clicked on, not an easy-to-push button right where the thumb goes.
Don't buy this. It is a product design failure

Meh, not that great.. my baby is 6 months old and it has lasted so far. coverage is somewhat spotty (our house is not that large- 1800 sq ft) and the video feed occasionally flashes. video quality leaves something to be desired. sound starting to go out periodically as well.

you can probably get a higher quality product for the same price. I would keep looking

Don't waste your money!. Out of all monitors I have owned it is the most expensive and worst one I have had. The picture quality is very disappointing, even in daylight and the (lack of) reception and buzzing sound it makes are really unacceptable. I had very high hopes for this camera but it is extremely disappointing.  I had to buy a Summer monitor (for half the price) as I just could not rely on the Ovia. I could hardly make out my baby when he was sleeping and the buzzing next to my bed of the monitor (on level 2) made me crazy

Minimally functional.. Poor picture quality- we have used a crib and a pack n' play, and it's almost impossible to see the baby in them at night.  Also, annoyingly turns itself off without warning when the battery is at all low.  Since the battery doesn't last a super long time, this has happened to us several times.  Since there's no warning or signal, you don't know until you look at the monitor.  We don't use the music or talk back features, so those aren't of much value to us.  We really just want to be able to see and hear our baby consistently.  This is minimally functional, but that's about it

No sound!. This is a pointless monitor. The sound, at the max level, is so low you cannot hear anything. I returned it thinking it was defective. I received another one and it had the same issue. I would not pay a dollar for this thing

Pick a Different One!. I purchased this monitor with the extra camera to replace my Summer Infant Boost, which had a shattered screen from dropping it on the floor. I was excited to unpack it and put it to use, but it was a major disappointment. First of all, the cameras are huge compared to the Summer cameras. The monitor handset felt cheap compared to the Summer one, and it had an external antennae that you pull up on top, which I didn't like. The interface is NOT a touch screen, and you use the buttons on the side to change options. There are no instructions included in the box, and it was necessary to go on their website to download them as the interface was not intuitive to figure out.

Once I set everything up, I was frustrated to notice that one of the cameras kept cutting in and out on the monitor. Its signal would often not be picked up. In addition, if I had the handset near my computer or cell phone, it wouldn't take a signal from either camera. This is a big issue for me, as I plug the monitor in at night right next to my phone. There was no dual view for the two cameras. I could have it autoscan every few seconds between the rooms, or I could put it up on multiview (which is a quad view). Since we were only using two cameras instead of four, much of my screen space was blank it was hard to see the baby. Perhaps the worst part of this monitor was the terrible volume. When my baby woke from her nap screaming her head off, I could barely hear her. Our Summer monitor is so much louder than that - it can wake you just from her moving around some.

Another pretty bad feature were the lullabies. It sounded nice in theory, and would be really helpful for the newborn stage. However, while my baby was napping, the lullabies randomly started playing! I went back in the system to ensure that they were off, and they sure were. It could have turned out really poorly if it woke her up while she was sleeping.

The only positives I had for this monitor are that the picture quality and zoom were a little better than the Summer. I would look elsewhere for your monitoring needs

broke quickly - wouldn't recommend. It seemed to work okay at first but then the sound started cutting out intermittently. The sound wouldn't come on until my child was crying for a minute or two. I tried tinkering with the features and adjustments thinking I had inadvertently turned down the sensitivity. I was hoping I would work it out. Now it doesn't produce any sound at all. The picture is now cutting in and out too. I'm pretty disappointed in this product

Defective Audio, Poor Video. My unit seems to have a problem with microphone. The audio sensor is picking up sound where there is none. The means when the child is actually making noise, we don't really know it unless we happen to be looking at the display at the time. It also means we cannot use the monitor in VOX mode.

Aside from that, the video quality is fairly poor. The daytime video is somewhat sharp, but movement is very choppy. The night vision is just a garbled blur. Very little detail whatsoever. You can see movement, but not much else

Screen completely blutty after  few days. After a few days we noticed that picture was getting blurry. Every day it got worse. After about 10 days it got to the point that we could not see anything other than blur, fuzz and vertical scratch like lines ALL over the screen. Bought this monitor due to amazing reviews but I couldnt return it fast enough

Great Camera, BUT.... Oh, the camera quality was definitely better quality than what we have right now. The detail was AMAZING! I could almost see every hair on her head, even in night vision mode. Albeit the picture, as good as it was was distorted, like it made everything in the picture fat, like it was stretching the image. Here's why I returned it- We have a complete wireless set up for almost everything and have multiple wireless devices working at one time, not to mention microwaves and streaming devices. All this was apparently an overload for this monitor because it had this weird flickering thing it did on the monitor which constantly had me worried we were going to lose the connection. The worst part was that the sound kept cutting in and out like every 5 seconds. It just felt like we were never going to be able to keep a secure solid connection, so despite the awesome video quality we returned it to stick with the monitor we have now, Samsung, which we have had now for almost a year and a half with no connection issues or sound disturbances

extra features are weird and very user un-friendly. we had an old school summer infant monitor with a straight up 4" tv monitor. it was big but it was great, clear screen. I loved it but it crapped out - it was kind of old though.
the reasons I don't like this for the following reasons:

Good screen size, but that's about it.... I was excited when the baby video monitor arrived, but this video camera is only okay.
Pros:
Screen size
Ok picture
Built in music (5 settings, you better hope your newborn likes one of the five)

Cons:

I would not pay $170 or so for the camera. I think this was on sale around Black Friday for $99. Not worth it - so many better monitors out there!. This monitor is not worth it - there are many better products out there. I have had a couple different montiors and I found this one to be very bulky, not very user friendly/self explanatory (display buttons, menu, etc.) and the tilt on the camera to be very poor. I was very excited about getting this product, but in the end it proved to be very dissapointing and inconvenient to use. The only advantage is the size of the screen and the extra battery and charging station that comes in the package. I have gone back to my motorola MBP36 - this doesn't even come!

Fatal flaw - can't look down. This is an excellent video monitor if your baby sleeps on a high shelf or better yet the ceiling. It can look up - all the way up! - but not down. We experimented with every possible way to tilt and position it including titling down into crib (required duct tape, saran wrap, and a baby that can't reach) and hanging upside down (shelf to screw it into). None will give you the picture in the product ad. Ugh.  You get what you pay for.... So, rather than spending the $175 for another one of the monitors I KNEW worked well, I purchased this one on Black Friday for $75....  big mistake.  It's honestly just terrible.  The picture is bad, and if the camera is ANY distance at all from the crib (ours is on a shelf, about 6 feet from the mattress), it honestly looks as if the baby isn't even IN the crib (it's that hard to see). I'm looking for a new monitor to replace this one. It's just junk, in my opinion

worked for 30 min. I have purchased SEVERAL baby monitors around this price point, hoping to find one that will do a descent job. I was by far happiest with this monitor until it stopped working properly. Within 30 minutes of use, the screen went from clear and bright to dark and fuzzy, leaving only a strip of bright picture at the very top and around where the temperature is displayed. The monitor works much better when lights are on, unfortunately I need it for use when my baby is sleeping. When the receiver is on the base or free standing the picture looks completely black. Picking it up and changing the angle helps some but still extremely difficult to discern the picture

Video monitor. The display monitor is always on...no way to turn it off and it is very bright.  It is hard to sleep with the bright display monitor lighting up the room. The clip that can be used to attach the display monitor to your pants while you walk around is flimsy and falls off easily. There's been an orange light that popped up on the receiver recently and we can't get it to turn off

Movement is limited. Got this on a lighting deal before Christmas. It does what it advertises. The control is nice, big screen, not overly complicated. My main and really only problem is that it doesn't have full range of motion. If there was a way to invert the image/control it would be fine. You can move side to side, and up just fine. But try to move it down, good luck. This is problematic, because I would guess most people would want to put the camera above, not below or at level with the baby's crib. I wound up mounting mine on its side and it works somewhat. Would not have ordered if I had it to do over.
2.5 stars
poor audio quality. We have purchased and tested over 13 different video monitors, and the only one that doesn't hiss so loud I can't hear my baby is the Levana Stella

terrible video quality. Great price, but when buying a video monitor you expect to be able to actually see your little one. Not the case with this product!!! The video quality is the worst I have ever seen!
Love the talk feature and the portability, but the video quality negates all positive aspects.
I opened the box and foolishly threw away the box. If not, this item would be returned!!

No Option for additional camera. After much frustration and a few hours of searching I found a chart that shows which additional cameras are available for the Levana Jena video monitor. If you purchased your monitor "after December 1st, 2013" there is currently no optoin for an additional camera.

Levana technical support is non-existent. Phone support is currently not an option. They simply request that you go to another website to open a case and someone will get back to you within 2 to 3 days.

This is very good monitor. The sound quality is excellent compared to other video monitors we have purchased. The build quality is above average. It does not feel cheap in your hand. The video quality is decent. The frames per second is low so it does lead to some 'choppiness' but the color quality is very good. Over all features on the parent module are well thought out if not excessive. You'll never need more features then what are on this monitor. That being said, one star for a monitor that claims to support additional cameras but doesn't have them for purchase
Horrible video, all around.. The video quality is very poor and choppy. We went back to using our old video monitor (without video) and just use the audio

Do you want to SEE your kid on the monitor? If yes, do not buy this.. After three years of heavy use, our Summer Infant video monitor's night vision light burned out but even without it's video capability, that monitor is better than this one. The video quality has an awful delay, making it look like a grainy, out-of-focus recording. A far cry from the crystal-clear quality of the Summer Infant monitor. It's truly awful. I mean, you buy a *video* monitor so you can *see* your kid, right? Right. This doesn't provide that luxury. The name "video monitor" is a true misnomer.
Other issues:
The auto-off setting seems like a great power-saving option, but what they don't tell you is that the entire handset monitor shuts down if there's no sound near the camera. The Summer Infant monitor allowed us to turn the video off but still monitor by audio. With the Jena monitor, the whole thing shuts down. The sensitivity control setting didn't seem to change this much. Even at the highest sensitivity setting, the thing still shut down so I didn't have the option to listen if I wanted to. Call me crazy, but hearing the silence in my kid's room is soothing and let's me know she's really out. A monitor that has turned itself off tells me nothing but that it sucks.

The nightlight and lullaby options on this monitor just weren't useful for us. The fact that the controls were right on the handset where you could (and we did) easily bump them (inadvertently turning on music that wakes your child) is just a bad design.

The camera is (aside from the terrible quality) well-designed: small, simple, and very stable. It isn't very adjustable, basically just moving up and down with no swiveling. Not a big deal for us since we set it on a bookcase across the room, but if we wanted to hang it on the wall high up, I don't think it would have been adjustable enough. It was nice that it could run on just batteries so that you didn't have a cord hanging down if you did hang it on the wall, though.

The video quality (or lack thereof) was what really killed this monitor for us but after playing with it a bit, all of the other little annoyances reared their ugly heads. Avoid this lousy product. Pay more for better quality

sound volumne not loud enough. We tried all sorts of things to get the sound louder moving the monitor closer etc.  Nothing worked and so we be returning. I'm grumpy about this system.. I like this baby monitoring system far better than the previous one I purchased. (The Infant Optics DVR-5 2.4 GHz Digital Video Baby Monitor with Night Vision-it died after 10 months and I wrote a review concerning that). Anyway, the things I like about this system is the "Vox" feature which basically shuts the system down unless it hears sounds from your baby's room and then it turns back on for 10 seconds, longer if your baby continues to make noise. This is fantastic because my other system did not do this and I was listening to my child's white noise machine all night through the monitor, which was set to the "rain" setting and I truly believe it subconsciously caused me to have to get up in the middle of the night to relieve myself. I also appreciate the variety of settings on the VOX feature which allows it to NOT go off due to the noise of my child's white noise machine. Secondly, I like the fact that I can talk to my child through the monitor and reassure her that's 'It's ok, I'm getting more batteries for the white noise machine' when the white noise machine fails to run. Thirdly, I like the night vision setting so that I can brighten the picture on the monitor or darken it, depending on my mood. The only con I have is that the picture is not perfect, it's good, but sometimes I can't tell where my child's head is in her crib.

Bottom Line: to anyone who is debating getting a video monitoring system over and audio one, get it. It's really reassuring to be able to look at your child any time you want to. I'd go as far as saying it is as important as the white noise machine. Furthermore, I've only had two baby monitoring systems, but this one is FAR better than the other one

Low Quality, Poor Features. I purchased this monitor as a replacement for a well-functioning Summer Infant Slim and Secure monitor. I am having a hard time coming up with any pros for this item other than that the 'on' switch functions properly.

Cons from the child's perspective:
1. Very bright green light on the camera. So bright it casts shadows in the room. My child had trouble ignoring the constant glow.
2. Incredibly loud intercom volume. This is Not adjustable. Rather than reassuring my child, the intercom terrified him.

Cons from a parent perspective:
1. There is no continuous audio monitoring without keeping the video on. The only option for turning the very bright monitor off is the Vox feature, which triggers the monitor to come on when noise is detected in the child's room. The problem is that the monitor is completely dark and silent in between. The battery died one night, and we didn't even know it. After that, we left the audio/video on constantly, but had trouble sleeping with the light.
2. The button to play lullabies (loudly) in the child's room is very easily triggered and located on the side of the handheld monitor. We repeatedly accidentally pressed this button while grabbing for the monitor in the dark. This resulted in our child being woken repeatedly at 2 or 3 am by loud nursery music.

We have returned the unit and will be purchasing a second Summer Infant unit for our new baby

Also, despite having good visibility during the day and night - the angles this requires are just impractical. Its a fairly heavy unit that when hung on the wall has some seriously limiting views.

My humble opinion says this camera is NO WHERE near worth the asking price because it just doesn't function nearly as well as a higher end model (I truly love my samsung baby monitor) and also for the lack of high end features (such as wi-fi). Good in a bind, and might be okay (I brought it with me on a cross country trip to nana's) for part time use - but I would return this if I had bought it because overall - not worth the $ when their are so many better options out there

Great for Day, but not for Night. We had a Summer infant video monitor for our oldest daughter and then used it for our middle daughter. We would still be using it for our third daughter, but after 6 years it finally stopped working properly. We did not want to spend a great deal of money, so after many hours of reading reviews and looking at many video monitors we bought this one. I was very excited when we received it and it worked great for during the day, but things all changed at night. Our daughter sleeps with a white noise machine and the monitor picks that noise up, so it is very loud. We tried turning the VOX sensitivity down, the monitor would not turn on when she cried. We woke up to a screaming 4 month old who was soaked in her tears, which made me feel terrible. I noticed that the power light on the camera was shining right in her eyes, so we decided that she would sleep back in our room for the night. The next night we covered the power button with tape and left the camera on all night. The camera is very bright, so I had to turn it away from me while I was sleeping. Our daughter does not cry very loud, so it is very difficult to hear her over the white noise. When we did have the VOX on the camera turns on and off all the time because of the white noise. We are very disappointed, so we are sending it back. We need a camera that lets us sleep with our baby in another room and not have to worry about not hearing her or being kept awake because the monitor is so bright and loud. Let the research for another monitor begin!!

Not nearly as good as the 'lesser' Astra model. My wife and I have owned the Levana Astra baby video monitor for three months now, and being our first video monitor it's completely changed the way we monitor our youngest daughter. Unlike with our old audio monitor, which only offered vague audio hints at what was occurring in her room, at any time we can pick up the video monitor and have a clear view of what is going on in her room and what she's up to. We decided to get a second system to keep in my office for monitoring our young dog in the living room who loves to chew everything.

The monitor has four buttons along with a 4-button control pad. The first button is probably our favorite feature... the intercom, which allows you to speak through the camera. In the mornings, when my daughter wakes up, my wife can let her know "I'll be right there", or during the day, when my two daughters are playing, if I see something that could be unsafe, I can inform them "please don't do that" without me leaving my desk.

The second button allows you to control the movement of the camera... when pressed, you can remotely pan and tilt the camera using the control pad to see anything in the room. The third button brings you to a menu that'll allow you to set various options such as screen brightness and sound sensitivity. Lastly, the fourth button below the control pad allows you to zoom in on an object in a single step. Pressing up or down on the control pad allows you to cycle through cameras if you have more then one. Pressing left or right allows adjusting the volume.

Pressing the power button allows you to turn off the screen and use the monitor for audio-only, which is useful at night when there's no reason to have the screen on, illuminating your bedroom. There's the option to play three different lullabies through the intercom speaker. This would have been an absolute DREAM when both my daughters were babies, as they both loved lullabies when going to sleep, but none of their toys played them for more then 10 minutes at a time... which meant going back into the room and turning the music back on if they didn't fall asleep fast enough. Lastly, there's the option to connect up to three other Levana camera's for a total of four being viewed on one monitor. Selecting 'sequential view' on the menus allows you to cycle through the cameras automatically.

Levana Stella (32018) vs Astra (32006)
--------------------------------------
This model (Levana Stella 32018) is Levana's top model, according to their website, while our current monitor is their second best. You would never have guessed that from using both...

Physical Comparison: The Stella may have a .8" larger screen, however the monitor itself is much larger overall and weighs nearly 50% more. The Stella feels more like a portable game system, while the Astra easily fits into my back pocket. The Astra has a large fold-out kickstand centered on the back while the Stella has a small one offset to one side, making it a bit unstable. Both have fold-out antennas, however the Stella's is wobbly and has popped off twice. Quality-wise, the Astra beats the Stella easily.

Video Comparison: The biggest difference between the two models is the screen size... the Astra offers a 3.5" display with 320x240 resolution, while this model has a 4.3" display with 480x272 resolution. Unfortunately, bigger is not better... after finding that the Stella's video seemed a bit 'choppy', I checked the stats and found that this bigger monitor had a framerate of 12 FPS... less then half that of the Astra's 25 FPS! In addition, the on-screen icons of the Stella are completely different then the Astra's... the Astra has smooth icons, while the Stella uses groups of four pixels as 'blocks' to create rough 'Atari quality' icons. Looking at the 'X' on the screen of the Astra, it looks very smooth... on the Stella, it's jagged and you can clearly see it's made up of 9 'blocks'. In addition, the Astra's icons are black and clearly visible at all times, while the Stella's icons are grey and easily blend into the background, making them almost invisible at times. In full brightness, the colors are only slightly better for the Stella, but the Astra is MUCH sharper. Neither monitor offers as vivid an image as the pictures above show, but since these are not for capturing memories, the quality is good enough for me. Overall, the 'lesser' Astra looks a WHOLE LOT better.

Audio Comparison: Audio seems to be exactly the same quality between the two models. The only functional difference between the two overall is the ability to adjust the volume of the lullabies on the Stella... an option that my wife and I both liked. The Astra's lullabies are set at a fixed volume.

Functional Comparison: As mentioned, the only functional difference between the two is the ability to control lullaby volumes on the Stella... otherwise the Stella offers no additional features. However, the functions on the Stella don't work nearly as well as on the Astra. First, the camera pan and tilt... the Astra's controls are smooth for both panning and tilting the camera, while the Stella's is horrible, and by far its worst feature. Panning side to side is the same as on the Astra, but tilting up and down is WAY too sensitive... press the 'up' button for a split second too long, and you're looking at the ceiling. I found it very difficult at times to center one a specific target as it can be 'jumpy' at times. Press the 'zoom' button on the Astra and you're instantly at 2x zoom... press it again and you're back... INSTANTLY. How could they screw up that? The Stella does... press the zoom button and you get an 'Enter zoom...' screen and 3 seconds later, you're zoomed in. Press it again, you get 'Exit zoom...' and 3 seconds later, you're finally back. I avoid the zoom function on the Stella like the plague...

Battery life, according to specs, is much better on the Astra (48 hours vs 36 hours). I also have had a bit of trouble with the Stella's signal... the signal seems to go out from time to time. Although it's very brief, it causes the video and controls to 'stutter' a bit. No such problems on the Astra. In addition, if the cameras are placed too close to one another, the Stella loses the signal and locks up, while the Astra still works fine. Placing the monitors within two feet of one another, the Stella goes dead... within one foot, both monitors lose their signals.

I tried using either camera with the other system's monitor, but despite 'finding' the other's camera, it won't display the camera's video. I also can't figure out how to remove a camera from either's monitor... possible bug, or simply undocumented procedure. I'll be contacting Levana to find out.

Unless you find yourself far from the monitor where you absolutely need a larger screen, I *HIGHLY* recommend avoiding this system and go buy the Lavana Astra. Despite a $55 difference in price (according to Lavana's website) the 'lesser' Astra system is a far, far better video monitor in nearly every aspect. I probably would have given this model an extra star, maybe even two, if we had not owned the Astra model and this was our first video system, however seeing how well a real video monitor can (and should) work, the Stella is an overpriced disappointment

Freezes on image of your peacefully sleeping child.... You're better off looking at photo of your child while she cries in next room, at least you'll get a better image. Basically, that's what happened to me twice with my last Summer Infant monitor experience. Problem with these units is that when they freeze, they freeze on their last image. So basically, you'll be looking at an image of your child sleeping peacefully when it reality, she may be crying (or worse) in the next room. The first time it happened, I set my monitor next to my laptop so I thought perhaps there was some kind of interference. But the second time, there was nothing.

No permanent damage was done other than making feel like the worst parent in the world, so I'm not suing Summer Infant, but I'm certainly going to make sure no one else buys one of their products unwarned. Maybe I'm overreacting. But this is my first child and I don't like feeling like I neglected my child.

I didn't buy this particular unit. I bought another video monitor by Summer Infant, then, when that one failed, I got a different model. Amazon doesn't seem to sell the model I got. But, since I got 2 different monitor models from Summer Infant and they both had the same flaw, I thought I'd comment to warn other buyers of Summer Infant video monitors.

Both units I got, at some point would freeze. When they did, instead of showing a blank screen, or warning of some sort, simply froze the picture, usually on an image of my baby sleeping. Now, I ask you, given the option of ways for a video monitoring unit to fail, what do you think is the worst possible way for the software to handle it? I'd think having the image freeze on an image of your baby sleeping peacefully is probably pretty close to the worst. I believe this is how all the bank heist movies get around video surveillance.

Twice with this monitor, my wife found my baby crying hysterically when it was my watch. Both times, the video had frozen showing a peacefully sleeping baby. Admittedly, both times, the unit was no longer transmitting sound, so if I had noticed that there was no longer any white noise coming from the unit, I would have noticed something was wrong. However, I think I'm not unusual in tuning out white noise, so I didn't notice when it stopped.

I'm not sure why the image froze instead of having a "no signal" image or something else. I know that there is that kind of message actually on the unit because I have seen that message. However, I noticed on the first unit that when it had a bad signal, it would "strobe" (jumping from one still image to another). I think that's how they try to make it seem like they have a stronger signal (by not blanking the screen, they show the last image until the next image comes through).

It's unfortunate because Summer Infant actually has great customer service. When my first unit died (it did the same thing, but I happened to have another monitor so I never missed my baby crying) they sent me a new unit with very little fuss. With that first unit, I got stuttering images, and then a freeze. As it turns out, you're not supposed to have video units in the same house together, so that might have caused that. But, anyway, in the end, the first unit wouldn't even show a picture at all, so it was genuinely defective.

However, now that 2 units have showed the same freezing flaw, AND I have been traumatized by my crying infant while simultaneously thankful that nothing serious happened during those particular times.

I don't know that ALL Summer Infant video monitoring systems do this. Maybe it was just these 2 units. Maybe it's a common flaw with all monitoring systems (I have another cheap system that I bought on Gold Box special, Lorex, as a backup that doesn't do this). All I know is that this seems STUPID, and DANGEROUS. I know enough about software and electronics to know that this is not a difficult problem to rectify and one that should be one of the most basic problems to anticipate and correct.

Having your baby in the other room crying while you watch TV behind closed doors isn't the worst thing that could happen to your child (feels like it though). And, parents have had to do this very thing in many sleep training techniques. However, those are generally deliberate actions. Having this happen while you are peacefully going about your business while counting on your video system to alert you to your baby's wellbeing is unacceptable.

Again, I don't have enough experience with monitors to know whether this is a common flaw. If it is, then I'm still giving this unit a 1 star rating (can't give 0 or negative) and I'd give all the other the same rating too. If you decide to buy this unit anyway, just watch out for this flaw. You can just imagine how bad it feels to find your baby crying hysterically and having no idea how long she's been crying

Liked it until it stopped working after less than a year.. This was our first monitor, and at first it was a lifesaver to have the ability to see what was going on in our baby's room. But the advantages ended there. There were some occasional static issues, and I did not like the fact that the video monitor lacks a low volume setting (just loud, less loud, or NO audio). Furthermore, the video monitor has a standby mode that supposedly cuts the video but retains the audio - problem is, while it does cut the picture, the screen is still "on," so there remains a bright glow that makes it useless to have in your bedroom. We finally just put the video monitor in the kitchen and kept the audio with us in the bedroom.

Also, the cords for the two monitors are pretty short, which limits where you can place them in any room, but the cord for the camera is much longer than it would ever need to be. Doesn't make sense.

But the real problem came at about the one year mark, when I went to turn off the audio monitor, to find that I cannot turn it off! We had not dropped it, had not moved it excessively. It simply would not shut off! I opened it up to see what was wrong, and there is nothing wrong. Nothing snapped off, nothing is blocking it . . . it simply will not turn off! So, now I have a monitor that I will never be able to turn off unless I physically remove the battery every time I'm not using it.

To top it off, customer service would NOT refund. They would not replace the unit without charging us an additional $50 (for which we get a USED monitor, not a new one). If a product is going to be this shoddy, they should at least be willing to replace it without this hassle.

It's a real shame, because I would have told anyone beforehand that this was a worthwhile purchase, even with the former complaints. But this lack of respect for the consumer after the product breaks is completely inexcusable and renders the product entirely worthless. This company should be ashamed of itself and it's useless customer "service." Caveat Emptor, indeed!

Cons:
Volume control - Only offers a few predefined settings. You adjust the volume by clicking a plus and minus button. No knob. The lowest volume setting is still extremely loud. If you plan on using any kind of white noise maker, fan, or infant bedtime music player in the childs room, prepare to lose some sleep if this monitor is set up beside your bed. You will hear every little sound in that room amplified at an annoying level.

Reception - Spotty at times even at close distance with few obstructions between camera and monitor. Seems like the least little thing interferes with the signal. If a person sits by the video monitor or walks by, the signal becomes scrambled and makes a loud noise which you can't turn down (see above).

Power cord - Became loose and unusable at both ends after 18 months of use. I repaired the end that plugs in to the back of the monitor by splicing (soldering) in a connector from a different power supply. Now the end that plugs in to the outlet is borken. Had to order another powers supply from Summer ($20).

Overall - I would not recommend this monitor

It's a shame. Not only are we out $100+ we actually really liked the way the camera functioned for the short time it was working as advertised.

Looking at a lot of other folks experience/ratings here, in seems like there's enough people with similar issues that it really comes down to the quality of, or lack thereof, the product. Sorry, iBaby, we'll never take a chance with your products again

The monitor is designed to fail within 300-500 charges (AKA as soon as your warranty ends. For the first year or so, this was a great product. Not the greatest night vision, but totally acceptable, and the battery held a charge. Right around the year mark, the battery started going downhill and we had to charge the monitor between nap time and bed time to ensure that it had enough juice to make it unplugged for a few hours before we went to sleep. By the 15 month mark, the product won't work at all unless plugged in to the wall, and it sometimes still turns off and entirely resets the system even when plugged in and charging. When I spoke with customer service, they indicated that the battery is designed to only charge 300-500 times and will die after that, leaving you to buy an entirely new $70 monitor (they don't offer just a battery replacement). AKA every time your monitor leaves the one year warranty period, you will then be obligated to buy a new $70 monitor since it won't even stay on when you have it actively plugged into the wall and charging. Might be a good business model for them to keep getting money, but it's an awful customer retention model. Rather than buying a new $70 monitor and being required to buy another one in a year and few months, I'll be taking my money elsewhere and buying an entirely new monitor that offers a replaceable battery if needed

The quality control on this product is inferior. You may get a good one or you may not. For $80 is it worth taking the chance?

Mac/Apple owner?? Buyer beware!! Won't be able to upgrade firmware, no customer service. This review is coming at the 2 year mark of ownership of this product. I just finished saying how much I loved this monitor/camera and how rare it is these days to still be loving a product 2 years down the road.

I spoke too soon.

We recently had our second child and decided to get a second camera, as this monitor/camera combo stated that it could pair up to 5 cameras. What they don't tell you, anywhere in the description, is that you MUST have a Windows operating system to update the Firmware, which is required to pair and add any additional camera. This being despite the fact that on their website, they state that it is comparable with Mac OS and they have Mac OS firmware downloads. As their super unhelpful customer service agent stated "yaaaa...we've been having issues with Macs, you gotta have a PC...sorry."

Now, Eufy is in part considered a home security company. It should give ANY customer or new parent concern if a security tech company cannot figure out how to update their products' Firmware on a Mac. This is computing 101, and for a tech company...not a good sign.

So anyway, we asked if they could instead ship us out a monitor/camera set that is pre-paired to overcome this idiotic issue. No dice. Their solution? Go buy a PC, sorry, we can't help you further.

So now what? Stuck with an ugly paperweight? Amazon won't return the monitor since it is outside of their return window. What useless customer service and now useless product.

Again ------ beware if you actually care about security. Firmware updates are usually necessary to keep your cameras and devices up-to-date with the latest patches to prevent unauthorized access. If a company selling these devices can't figure out how to have these firmware updates installed, that should be a HUGE red flag.

And if you don't know, now you know

Getting a reply to any given message frequently took days, and the reps' suggested solutions actually made the problem worse. Efforts to call iBaby's listed customer service number provided an even more uniquely horrendous outcome: all calls go directly to voicemail DURING the company's stated business hours; and, wait for it, one time that I called, THE MAILBOX WAS FULL.
Feeling stranded with a very expensive dud monitor and a baby just around the corner that I'd need to be able to keep an eye on, I resorted to pestering the company anyway I could to provoke a response. I emailed, called, sent a message to their Facebook page. At long last someone from iBaby wrote back to me again, and arranged a call a time that was mutually agreeable. Now, to be fair to iBaby, I missed this first call because my wife went into labor unexpectedly early. It's now been a full month since I first contacted iBaby, my daughter has arrived, and I've received no resolution from them regarding the paperweight I hoped to use to remotely monitor her. Go ahead and buy an M7 Lite or any of iBaby's suite of products. Just know that when you do so, their warranty isn't worth the time it took their lawyer to write it

- Customer service seemed keen on making the issue my fault so while I think it is likely there is a defect it is apparent that I would have needed to go to some effort to prove it just to get an RMA. I Would Not Buy Again. I've had an iBaby for 5 years now, spanning two babies. I've owned the M7, the M6T, and the M6.

First, the good. Picture quality is actually quite good, as is the night vision. Some of the features are well-designed (but poorly executed, more on that later), and some of the features are actually useful.

It's not an awful device, but it's not a good one, either. Connecting your phone to the device can be awful. For whatever reason, sometimes it works, and sometimes it doesn't work. Sometimes it doesn't work for weeks on end, and then 2 weeks later you'll try again on a lark, and out of the blue, you connect. Sometimes it'll work for months on end, you'll put your baby to sleep, and out of the blue, it stops working. And you're SO looking forward to walking into the nursery and wake the baby up by fiddling with the stupid baby monitor, right?

Android users are definitely a second-class citizen with iBaby. They claim Android support, and we do have an iBaby app in the store, but for whatever reason, their support seems to think that iPhone users are the defacto standard for iBaby. Here's an excerpt of a conversation I had with their customer support:

"OK, I'm sorry you're having so much trouble connecting your Android phone. Can you try your iPhone, please?"
"I use Android."
"Oh, I see. Can you borrow someone's iPhone or iPad?"
"Are you serious? You're asking me to go over to my next door neighbor and ask for his phone?"
"Yes."

Security... we're all scared of people hacking into our baby cams. I've taken a look at their security setup, and honestly, it's much too complicated for me to assess what kind of risk there is. This isn't necessarily a BAD thing, but I have to wonder if they could've just used a much simpler setup. As it stands, both Amazon cloud services and some kind of P2P server owned by ... who(?!?) are both involved in the communication between your phone and your iBaby device. Is it secure? Who know! They say it is, but there seems to be a lot of middlemen between you and your device, and Amazon doesn't have the greatest reputation when it comes to user privacy. One thing is for sure. Buying this device lets Amazon know you have a baby. I guarantee you, that fact will be in your "Amazon shopper profile". I really love Amazon for being consumer friendly, but at the same time, I know they're in the marketing business.

I've had two iBabys get bricked. Both times, life was good for a long time, and then out of the blue, and I lost all ability to connect. iBaby was not forthcoming with the details, but from some web sleuthing I was able to piece together that in both cases, iBaby Labs pushed out a software update that, for whatever reason, didn't get applied correctly. Both times it bricked my device. To iBaby Lab's credit, they send a new device both times, however, the second time, it took them over a month to get the new device to me, and that was only after I threatened them with asking my credit card company to reverse the charges.

Last bad thing about iBaby: the sound. The sound is dreadful. Listening to your baby isn't awful... I would characterize it as "OK". The sound stream is too compressed for my liking; it would be nice if you could configure the compression of the audio stream. However, talking TO your baby, and playing music for your baby is just.... awful. Truly awful. So bad that one has to wonder ... "why bother with that feature?" It's hard to believe that the company presented this device to a focus group and everyone agreed "Oh, yeah. The sound quality is sufficient!" Nope! It's dreadful.

There are some decent features to the device, but the latest models are stuffed with garbage features. Stuff that's obviously designed to justify a higher pricetag. This review is getting long, so I'll leave it at that. You'll see for yourself. I'm pretty sure the humidity reading is wildly wrong.

Last word: I really wish this device weren't round. Surely they could've figured out a way to implement 360 degree rotation without making the thing round! So inconvenient!

(+) Access to camera via WiFi and on iOS
(+) Ability to control settings and camera remotely

(-) Poor ergonomics. Awkward shape requires planning of the camera’s placement. When the camera rotated around it’s axis, it expands the overall footprint. The base is also in the way of the camera in some positions and needlessly attaches/detaches.
(-) The camera can only move in macro adjustments vertically and horizontally in about 10 degree increments. The software does not allow for fine adjustments, nor a ‘point to center’ functionality with a paired phone.
(-) The camera defaults to 640p resolution, despite being set to 1080p in the settings. You have to check the settings every time then close out and only then will the camera feed switch to 1080p.
(-) The camera will intermittently only display pink spectrum and cannot be corrected until the unit is unplugged and then plugged in again.
(-) The thermometer is off by + 4°F. I have compared the temperature to a thermocouple probe I already have (confirmed accuracy with several other temperature probes throughout the house) and it states the temperature in the baby room is 69°F, whereas the iBaby monitor states that it is 73°F.
(-) Rotating the night light rotates the entire unit, including the camera. This not only makes it difficult and dizzying to monitor the baby, but the entire unit will slightly move on the shelf (due to vibration?) and does not reset to the exact position. Due to the lack of fine adjustments, the camera cannot be placed back to the ideal viewing angle without moving the entire unit back to the initial position.
(-) Questionable resolution. I’ve attached two photos, one with 1080 resolution on an iPhone camera and one from the iBaby while settings confirm 1080p. The iPhone is much sharper, which calls into question if the iBaby is actually transmitting at 1080p. My internet connection tests at over 107Mbps currently, so I can’t see how it would be WiFi limited

The hardware is attractive and has a few helpful features for using a camera due monitoring, but are poorly designed as a baby monitor.

First, the standard base is just a flat plate. Since you shouldn't put it in the crib with the baby, you will either use the monitor from an elevated position, far away from the baby or be required to purchase the wall mounting clip. I chose the former option as I still didn't want cables dangling over the crib, and this mode of use really cuts down on the effective resolution of the video.

Second, and most annoyingly, the apps for Android and iOS are disgraceful. They crash constantly and do not produce similar results on different operating systems. Support from the company translates to advice to improve your Wi-Fi connection speed, which does not help when you have poorly designed and poorly maintained applications. For example, on the iPhone, if you zoom in, you lose the ability to pan. If you return to the app after the motion alert is triggered, there is no video.

The sensitivity settings are not useful. On the iOS version there are five different markings for sensitivity but only three actual settings. All of them are too sensitive. A slight movement by the baby triggers the alert. Another blatantly omitted feature... If I am in the room to tend to a crying baby, how come there is no easy way to turn off the alert so that my phone does not go off constantly in my pocket... when I am in the room. The only way to do that quickly is to pull the power cord out of the device or navigate three levels through the options to silence the alert triggers.

Also, why must the alert levels be the same level on every user's device? My wife and I can have different thresholds and perhaps we don't want to both be notified for every jerk.

I also take issue with the video and picture taking capability. A device in my house snapping pictures of my child somehow produces pictures that are forever watermarked with a 'shared by ibaby'. I am sorry ibaby, that's not your property; stop ruining the photos. My Canon camera does not drop a Canon logo in the bottom right of every frame, but why do you think you should?

The support I received for continual availability issues are laughable. Unlike a traditional monitor, there is no guard against false positives! If the app cannot connect to the monitor (yes, I know, to the ibaby cloud), you simply get no notifications, rather than being informed that there may be an issue. Ignorance with a baby is not the default option I would choose.

In the end we bought a Philips Advent audio monitor, which we use constantly, and the ibaby is an overpriced security camera in the baby's room
