AVOID THIS. Decent camera tied to a horrific app. Used so much background data I got charged by my carrier. This camera is really cute, has great rotation ability, and is rather easy to set up. However, it locks you into using an Android app (I can't say if the iOS app is better) that was designed to produce a terrible user experience. As an Android developer I know how hard it is to build a large-scale app with lots of features, but this app is just a circus.

The Major issues:
- There seems to be no way to export photos and videos from the app. It has a built in library, but I manage my own files, thank you. I plan to keep baby pictures long after I stop using a babycam.
- The app can work on local WiFi, or mobile data. It can't, however work on WiFi that's not on the same network as the camera. Do these developers not realize how common it is to have WiFi when you're not at home? This is a primary use case.
- The app continues to use mobile data when you're not using it. I looked at it for a few seconds and then closed the app. The next day I find it used 3.5GB of background data from WiFi (not really a problem) and 1.5GB of mobile data (which is a HUGE problem. In ONE DAY. It had nothing that it needed to do! I got charged $15 for data overages on day 3 of my monthly cycle. WTF iBaby? Are you going to reimburse me for my losses caused by your inexcusably poor app?

The minor issues I could probably get over:
- Video quality is not very good for the price range this is in. I've had better results with $80 IP cameras. This one offers convenience and a service, but I'd still like the video to be somewhat on par. Maybe it's just the poor app, but I know it's not my phone.
- Video takes too long to load, even when at home and on WiFi. A 7-13 second delay isn't what I want out of a baby monitor
- Motion/sound alerts don't combine, they just produce dozens of separate alerts on your phone that drown out any other notifications (because they happened every few seconds when I was testing it). Only a minor issue because I can turn off motion/sound notifications.

The good:
- It's cute - my wife was going to paint it like BB8.
- Setup was pretty simple, and I didn't have to poke a hole in my firewall to use it out of the house

Great product with two MAJOR flaws. This is a great product with two major flaws.

Pros -
-very easy setup (make sure you are using the 2.4GHz band and not the 5GHz if your router has dual bands
-very reliable - we had no issues that were due to the iBaby... any issues were from the router and were easily fixed
-app works great - this is the best part... the iphone app is excellent (I assume android as well) - it is easy to use, quick to show the video, easy to set alerts, and requires a reasonably small amount of bandwidth (ie, don't use it all day on cellular, but it won't eat your data for the month if you check it from time to time)

Cons -

minor - no OSX or desktop app that I can find. I think people can run emulators for android to get it to work but on OSX I haven't had any luck albeit with very little effort.

major - it can't look down - of course it can't turn 360 in all directions, but you'll never have your baby monitor under the bed, so why did they allow it to look directly up and not down. This makes it very difficult to use on a shelf above the crib. Ours is above the door on a shelf of it's own and we had to prop it up with paint stir sticks to get it to see the entire bed on the other side of the room. This wouldn't be a problem if they had wall mounting hardware but they do not and with the way it connects I do not believe it will be able to be mounted sideways so that it would ever be able to look down.

major - it has a bright blue light that flashes rapidly at random intervals - blue light is the worst wavelength of light for sleep, as I assume everyone knows. Parents are supposed to limit exposure to blue light wavelengths for at least 30 minutes (some studies say longer) before the child is supposed to be going to bed. Now, we have a wifi indicator which irregularly flashes a bright blue LED all night in our daughter's room. In a dark room it's a pretty significant light. I have spoken with iBaby about it and they were willing to RMA my unit and give me one without the new light for a 20% restocking fee. So they apparently make units without the blue light but decided to put it in for some units. Note, there is already a wifi indicator light next to the plug in the back. It is read and flashing when it is connecting or not connected to a network and glows green when it's connected. This is fine, it's not distractingly bright, and green light is fine for sleep. I cannot get them to explain to me why they put in a redundant wifi indicator in a horrible color for sleep. Their remedy was to tape over the entire bottom of the unit (the area responsible for heat dissipation and where the speakers are located. I would return the unit if I could but we got it 3 months before our daughter was born and we are past the point of return. This may seem minor, but if you have a white shelf that it sits on, white walls or a white ceiling, then the the unit will light up the entire corner. This is such as easy fix for them. If they fix this and the wall mount issue then it would be a 5 star item. I gave it two stars instead of one because it has a lot of good qualities if you use it during the day. Black, non-reflective tape on the surface it sits on will help reduce the blue, flashing light

POSSIBLE FIX FOR INTERMITTENT SIGNAL LOSS. I stumbled upon something that drastically affects the signal on this, and other units using the 2.4 GHz frequency band.
If you have wireless internet and your router is operating on 2.4 GHz this product could suffer severe and intermittent signal loss regardless of proximity of the monitor and camera. This is important especially if you want to take advantage of two or more cameras simultaneously. It's so bad I thought the unit was defective!
The only thing they'll mention in the FAQ is that turning off your router may help. This isn't always possible and it shouldn't be required. There's plenty of room in the spectrum for 4 channels for the baby monitor AND your wireless internet. We have a tri-band router with 5 GHz so I just moved all of our wireless devices over to that and it completely solved my problem. If you don't have the option you can log into the settings for your router and change the channel until the interference goes away. Trial and error is the name of the game as the camera doesn't show up on most spectrum analyzers.
Levana should address this with more information than "turn your router off". Maybe list the specific spectrum groups the camera typically operates on so we can configure accordingly! It might save them and, more importantly, the customers from unneeded returns and frustration.

This monitor should really be five stars, except for one annoying and rather fatal problem: you can't turn off the loud "out of range" beeping that occasionally sounds. This causes it to sound a very loud beep that easily wakes us up at night. Sometimes it only beeps once a night, sometimes it will beep once every twenty minutes or so. Terrible Range. This product did everything we needed it to: video, talk back feature, good battery, and a good advertised range. The VOX feature (where it goes to sleep until your baby makes a sound) actually works better than I expected. The video was pretty clear and the sound quality was good.

However, the first night we used it, multiple times it would start beeping to notify us that it lost the signal. The monitor was less than 30 feet from the camera and it would repeatedly lose the signal. We would have to turn it off, get out of bed and walk closer to the baby's room, turn it on again, and hope that it picked up the signal.

Based on this, we decided to return it after one night of use. We have a pretty small house, so if it can't consistently pick up the signal in our house, I don't know where it would work well

Incorrect advertising. While the product does have a good video quality many of the claims on the website are false or misleading. The 8 hour battery life is incorrect we are talking more like 4 hours with the screen on (on a good day). I also didn't leave it plugged in all the time but tried to exercise the battery at first to make sure I was getting the most out of it (still 4 hours most days. The peep setting is called the VOX setting and works poorly if you have a sound machine going in the room which most of us do, there is NOTHING that tells you this so it is nice to know. The music button on the side is awful because you can accidentally press it, while other functions like camera switch are buried in the menu. THE WORST thing is that they advertise is 500 ft signal. On their site they do have the disclaimer below:

"Optimum range is 150 feet when signal is passing through walls or floors. Microwave ovens (when in use) may cause signal disruption at close range. Buildings with metal frames may also cause signal disruption. Maximum transmission range is 500ft."

So essentially if you live in a house with walls or intend to go outside the actual range is 150 ft. Which means that you can go possibly go on your porch but playing outside with your other kids is a no go. Additionally for reasons I don't understand there are certain nights (when it is plugged in and not being moved) that it loses signal every so often which makes it beep annoyingly. So you are forced to decide if you should unplug it so you can sleep and keep the doors open or live with the beeping so can hear the baby better (which is why you bought it in the first place.

They additionally don't have a phone number to call for this model. You can call the number but they say that they have reduced the support with phone representatives and tell you to go to the website. Live chat works, it took roughly 30 mins for me to get connected to an agent.

With all that being said I would buy a different brand if I had to do it over again, but this one works OK
